submitted.rationale: Of the 3 measured compositions, index 14 (Al0.29Sb0.71) had the highest EQE at 0.0079%. Index 12 (Sb 0.61) gave 0.0024% and index 20 (Sb 0.89) gave 0.0002%, so EQE appears to peak around Sb ~0.7. Band-gap predictions agree: AlSbO4 and Al5Sb3O16 have wide gaps and cannot absorb 2.4 eV light, while Sb-rich mixed-valence oxides can.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE of 0.0002%, about 40x lower than index 14
Measured EQE of 0.0024%, lower than index 14
Dominated by wide-gap Al2O3, AlSbO4 and Al5Sb3O16, which cannot absorb 2.4 eV photons

consultations.verdict: Support: AlSbO4 (stable, hull 0) has HSE gap 3.65 eV, cannot absorb 2.4 eV photons; Sb-oxide phases (Sb6O13 2.05 eV, SbO2 1.67 eV) absorb at 2.4 eV. Sb-rich end is the most promising, so measure index 20 first.

Mixed: Al5Sb3O16 is also a wide-gap phase (3.74 eV), so Al-rich/ternary regions won't absorb 2.4 eV. Index 20 gave very low EQE, so I'm probing an intermediate Sb-rich composition (Sb 0.71), where a mixed-valence Sb oxide may still absorb and Al may help passivate.

Mild support: Al2Sb2O7 at 50:50 has a predicted gap of 1.04 eV, so compositions around ~0.4–0.6 Sb may absorb 2.4 eV light. EQE rose about 40x going from Sb 0.89 to 0.71, so moving further toward Al (index 12, Sb 0.61) follows that trend, and the GP-UCB also picks it.
